h: Cathedral Views, Lido Days and Alice
p: AirHop's spot on Midleton Industrial Estate Road sits on the western side of Guildford, close to the A3 and not far from Stag Hill, where Guildford Cathedral looks out over the town. It's a striking modern brick building, and the grassy slopes around it are good for a calm wander once everyone has come back down to earth.

Guildford has a fun link to Lewis Carroll, who spent time in the town and died here in 1898. Look out for the Alice Through the Looking Glass statue in the castle grounds, where Alice is climbing through the mirror. It's a lovely little photo stop, and the castle gardens around it are beautifully kept.

In the warmer months, Guildford Lido is a popular outdoor pool beside Stoke Park, and the park itself is a big open space with playgrounds and room to roam. If you'd prefer proper countryside, Newlands Corner and St Martha's Hill on the North Downs give huge views over the Surrey Hills, and they're only a short drive out of town.
Gardeners in the family will want to make time for RHS Garden Wisley, a few junctions up the A3, while Loseley Park to the south-west is a grand Elizabethan house with walled gardens.

One practical thought: the town centre is hilly and the one-way system can confuse first-timers, so it often pays to park once and walk. The station is well placed if you're coming by train from London, too.
If you're visiting on a Saturday, the cobbled High Street gets lively, so arrive early for a parking space and a calmer stroll.
